experiments.guard: knMd's FENCED-CODE branch escapes its content. Round 4's own new test comment claims it: 'fenced content is NOT run through knInline' and lines inside a fence are 'escaped verbatim (escHtml)'. But the only fenced fixture in the suite (tests/taskmodal_model.test.mjs, the round-4 blockquote+fence test) is `const x = 1;` and `**not bold**` — escHtml is the identity function on both, so the escHtml call inside the fence can be dropped entirely and that exact-output assertion still matches byte for byte. Drop it: a judge verdict or TODO.md brief containing a fenced block with `` (or any `<`/`&`) is spliced RAW into the review-timeline body and the brief pane — the same injection round 4 closed for the NON-fenced path (knInline's escHtml) is still open one branch over.

knMd's HEADING LEVEL. The briefHtml exact-output test's own comment names it explicitly as one of the things it guards — 'Regressing ANY of these (heading level, code wrapping, ...) changes this string and goes RED'. It cannot: every heading in every fixture in the suite is `###` (tests/taskmodal_model.test.mjs's `### OBJECTIVE` and `### H`), and no test anywhere contains an h1, h2 or h4 assertion. Pin the level to a constant 3: `# TITLE` and `#### detail` in a task brief both render as <h3>, collapsing the whole heading hierarchy the `#{1,4}` capture exists to preserve — a real regression for a brief pane whose headings are its only structure, and a screen-reader/outline regression too.

WIRING — the FOURTH knMd/knInline call site, and the one the PR names FIRST as the reason knowledge.js survives the strip. knowledge.js's new header says the renderer 'is reused verbatim by the Work view's task-detail modal (taskmodal.js/taskmodalmodel.js)'; taskmodalmodel.js's briefHtml is the line this PR edited (it dropped the 'brief.md' argument), and taskmodal.js:127 `_briefPane` is where it actually reaches the DOM. Rounds 3 and 4 wired three call sites through a real DOM (kanban.js:152, taskmodal.js:156, taskmodal.js:116) — this one was left. tests/taskmodal_model.test.mjs drives briefHtml only as a PURE function, and both DOM tests in tests/taskmodal_render.test.mjs pass items with no brief/body/raw, so briefSource returns null and _briefPane short-circuits to its 'No brief recorded' note before ever calling briefHtml. Dead-code the call (binding kept referenced, no unused-import noise): every task brief in the modal's wide column renders as literal escaped markdown source — `### OBJECTIVE`, raw `**bold**`, raw backticks — which is exactly the regression this PR's own comment says the call exists to prevent. Same DEFEAT_SHAPES #7 shape ('two callers, one guarded') that rounds 3 and 4 already fired on twice.

knMd's `*` bullet alternative. knowledge.js's own doc comment (rewritten in round 2's rework, and the thing the three list-structure tests were written to protect) states the contract in as many words: `listType` is "'ul' for a `-`/`*` run, 'ol' for a `1.`/`2.` run". Every list fixture added in round 2 uses `-` only; no test anywhere feeds knMd a `*` bullet. Narrow the character class to `-` alone: a brief or judge verdict written with `*` bullets (valid markdown, and what an agent writing a verdict may well emit) renders as a run of paragraphs with a literal leading asterisk instead of a <ul> — no list, no <li>, and the `*` visible to the reader.

knMd's blank-line check runs on the TRIMMED line (raw.replace(/\s+$/, '')), not on raw — this is why a whitespace-only separator line closes an open list exactly like a truly empty one. No existing fixture has a whitespace-only line; every blank-line fixture (`- a\n\n- b`) uses a genuinely empty line. Drop the trailing-whitespace strip: a whitespace-only separator (common when a brief is hand-edited or pasted through something that pads lines) no longer matches `line === ''`, falls through to the paragraph fallback instead, and renders as a spurious empty `

` wedged between the two lists instead of being treated as the blank separator it visually is.

knMd's ordered-list regex allows leading indentation before the digit (`/^\s*\d+\.\s+(.+)$/`), deliberately wider than the unordered regex right below it. No fixture anywhere feeds knMd an indented ordered item; every `1.`/`2.` fixture starts at column 0. Narrow the regex to `/^\d+\.\s+(.+)$/`: an indented ordered item (`  1. a`, the ordinary shape of a numbered step nested under a bullet in a TODO.md brief) no longer matches the ordered-item branch, falls through to the paragraph fallback, and renders as a plain paragraph with the leading spaces and the bare numeral visible instead of an <li> inside an <ol>.

knMd's list-kind switch, ol -> ul direction (round 5 negative control, not named by the round-5 finding). When a `1.` run is immediately followed by a `-` run with no blank line in between, closeList() must run before the new <ul> opens, exactly as round 2's guard already pins for the reverse (ul -> ol) direction. Dropping the closeList() call on this branch leaves the earlier `<ol class="kn-ol">` unclosed, merging the two lists into one malformed nested structure instead of two independently-closed ones.
